questions.question: The period of first five year plan was between ________.
questions.questionHtml: The period of first five year plan was between ________.
questions.solution: The first five year plan was launched by the government of India in 1951 with the aim of developing the economy and reducing poverty. The plan was based on the Soviet model of economic development and focused on agriculture, irrigation, power generation, and infrastructure.

questions.question: India's first five-year plan was launched in ______.
questions.questionHtml: India's first five-year plan was launched in ______.
questions.solution: India's first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951 by Jawaharlal Nehru with an outlay of Rs. 2069 crore. Its focus was on improving agriculture, public health, and achieving a 2.1% annual growth rate. The Indian government has since replaced the practice of formulating Five-Year Plans with a three-year action plan, seven-year strategy, and a fifteen-year vision document under the NITI Aayog.

questions.question: ________ five year plan of Government of India (2012-17) was India's last Five Year Plan.

questions.solution: The Twelfth Five Year Plan of the Government of India covered the period from 2012-2017. The Twelfth Five Year Plan aimed to achieve faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth. It focused on reducing poverty and improving the standard of living of the people.

questions.question: Planned economic development in India began in ______ with the inception of the First Five Year Plan
questions.questionHtml: Planned economic development in India began in ______ with the inception of the First Five Year Plan
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1951.

  • The planned economic development in India began in 1951 with the inception of the First Five Year Plan, theoretical efforts had begun much earlier, even before the independence.
  • It focused primarily on the development of the primary sector, specifically agriculture and irrigation.

Important Points

  • First Five-Year Plan was launched from 1951 to 1956, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru.
    • It was based on the Harrod-Domar model with a few modifications.
    • This plan was successful and achieved a growth rate of 3.6% (more than its target of 2.1%).
  • The duration of the "Eleventh Five Year Plan" was from 2007 to 2012, under the leadership of Manmohan Singh.
    • It was prepared by the C. Rangarajan.
    • The theme was towards faster and more inclusive development.
    • It achieved a growth rate of 8% against a target of 9% growth.

Key Points

  • India had a total of 12 Five-Year Plans, the last one being from 2012-2017.
  • In 2015, Prime Minister Narendra Modi dissolved the Planning Commission and replaced it with the NITI Aayog
  • The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) facts:
    • Formed: 1 January 2015
    • Chairman - Narendra Modi
    • Vice-Chairman - Dr. Suman Bery
    • CEO - Sh. BVR Subrahmanyam

questions.question: Whose name among the following is associated with the second five-year plan?
questions.questionHtml: Whose name among the following is associated with the second five-year plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis.

Key Points

  • 1956-61 was the duration of the Second Five Year Plan.
  • The Second Five Year Plan was based on Mahalanobis Model.
  • ​Its main focus was on the industrial development of the country.
  • P. C. Mahalanobis was a famous Indian statistician who founded the Indian Statistical Institute.
  • The plan lagged behind the target growth rate of 4.5% and achieved a growth rate of 4.27%.

Additional Information

  • The five-year plans were one of the central plans.
  • The plans were formulated and were financed by the central government.
  • These were launched in 1951, with the first five-year plans covering the years 1951-56.
  • There were three breaks in five-year plans during 1966-69, 1978-80, and 1991-92.
  • "Twelfth Five Year Plan" duration is from 2012 to 2017, and it was under the leadership of Manmohan Singh.
  • It was the last five-year plan because Niti Aayog replaced it with the planning commission.
  • Its main theme was “Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth”.
  • Its growth rate target was 8%.​

questions.question: What was the prime target of the first five-year plan of India?
questions.questionHtml: What was the prime target of the first five-year plan of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Development of agriculture.Key Points

  • First Five year Plan
    • 1st five-year plan was for the period of 1951 to 1956.
    • The prime target of the first five-year plan of India was the Development of agriculture.
    • The target Growth was 2.1 % and the Actual Growth was 3.6 %.
    • It was based on Harrod-Domar.
    • The influx of refugees, severe food shortage & mounting inflation confronted the country at the onset of the first five-year plan.

Additional InformationSecond Five Year Plan (1956-1961)

  • The second five-year plan is based on the so-called Mahalanobis model.
  • This was the USSR model Indianized by PC Mahalanobis, the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute and a close aide of Nehru.
  • This model is known to have set the statistical foundations for state-directed investments and created the intellectual underpinnings of the license-raj through an elaborate input-output model.
  • This Model suggested that there should be an emphasis on the heavy industries, which can lead the Indian Economy to a long-term higher growth path
  • Started Industrial Policy Resolution 1956.

Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966)

  • The Third 5 year Plan focused on agriculture & enhancement in the production of wheat, but the succinct Sino - Indian War in the year 1962 exposed flaws in the economy & shifted the spotlight towards the Defence industry.
  • On May 31 & June 1, 1961, the National Development Council considered the Draft Report on the Third Plan and generally approved it.
  • In the course of this period, India's economy must not only enlarge swiftly but must, in unison, become independent and self-generating.
  • This long-standing approach is projected to offer a wide-ranging design of expansion for the country's natural resources, industrial advance, and agricultural changes in the social structure & an incorporated scheme of regional & national development.

Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974)

  • The fourth Five Year Plan was the first plan launched by the Indira Gandhi government amid the pressure of drought, devaluation, and inflationary recession.
  • The country was fighting with population explosion, increased unemployment, poverty, and a shackling economy. In addition, the situation in East Pakistan (now independent Bangladesh) was becoming dire as the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 and Bangladesh Liberation War took place.
  • Funds earmarked for industrial development had to be used for the war effort.
  • The result was that this plan period was also no better than the third five-year plan.

questions.solution: The first Five-Year Plan in India started in 1951, aiming for balanced economic growth through centralized and integrated national programs. The Planning Commission, established in 1950, was responsible for formulating these plans, with the Prime Minister as the ex-officio chairperson. The initial plan focused on agriculture, while subsequent plans targeted various sectors like industry, education, and health. Inspired by the Soviet model, these plans emphasized public sector development.

questions.question: IPR-1956 laid the foundation of the ______ Five-Year Plan.
questions.questionHtml: IPR-1956 laid the foundation of the ______ Five-Year Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Second.Key Points

  • Industrial Policy of 1956
    • Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 (IPR 1956) is a resolution adopted by the Indian Parliament in April 1956.
    • It was the first comprehensive statement on the industrial development of India. 
    • It was regarded as the “Economic Constitution of India” or “The Bible of State Capitalism”.
    • The government revised its first Industrial Policy (i.e.the policy of 1948) through the Industrial Policy of 1956.
    • The 1956 Policy empha­sised the need to expand the public sector, to build up a large and growing coop­erative sector and to encourage the separation of ownership and management in private in­dustries and, above all, prevent the rise of pri­vate monopolies.
    • It provided the basic framework for the government’s policy regarding in­dustries till June 1991.

Additional Information

  • The Indian Planning Commission was established in 1950 to formulate and implement five-year plans for economic development in India.
  • The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.7% per annum and focused on the development of agriculture, industry, and infrastructure.
  • The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis model of economic development and aimed to achieve a growth rate of 4.5% per annum. It focused on heavy industries, particularly steel, and aimed to reduce the dependence on imports.
  • The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985) aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.2% per annum and focused on poverty alleviation, employment generation, and rural development.
  • The Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002-2007) aimed to achieve a growth rate of 8% per annum and focused on human development, infrastructure development, and regional development.

questions.question: From which Five - Year Plan period was the formulation and implementation of the Five - Year Plan discontinued by the Government of India?
questions.questionHtml: From which Five - Year Plan period was the formulation and implementation of the Five - Year Plan discontinued by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Twelfth Five - Year Plan.

Key Points

  • The Government of India discontinued the formulation of Five-Year Plans after the Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017).
  • This decision marked a significant shift in the planning process, transitioning from centralized planning to a decentralized framework.
  • The NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in January 2015, signaling the end of the Five-Year Plan era.
  • The Twelfth Five-Year Plan focused on "Faster, More Inclusive, and Sustainable Growth" but was the last of its kind as the government moved towards rolling plans and sector-specific strategies.
  • The discontinuation reflected a modern approach to policy-making, emphasizing flexibility and real-time monitoring over rigid long-term plans.

Additional Information

  • Planning Commission:
    • Established in 1950, it was responsible for drafting Five-Year Plans based on India's economic priorities.
    • It was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015 to promote a bottom-up approach to planning.
  • NITI Aayog:
    • Formed on January 1, 2015, it serves as a policy think tank for the Government of India.
    • It focuses on cooperative federalism, involving states in the planning process.
  • Rolling Plans:
    • Introduced as a replacement for Five-Year Plans, they allow for flexibility and periodic adjustments based on real-time needs.
    • These plans focus on sector-specific growth strategies rather than a fixed timeline.
  • History of Five-Year Plans in India:
    • The first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on agriculture and irrigation.
    • A total of 12 plans were implemented, with priorities shifting to industry, infrastructure, and social sectors over time.

questions.question: Which period in India is described as Plan Holiday?
questions.questionHtml: Which period in India is described as Plan Holiday?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1966 to 1969 which is described as Plan Holiday.

Key Points

  • Plan Holiday:-
    • The period from 1966 to 1969 in India is known as the Plan Holiday because during this time the government put a pause on the Five-Year Plans that had been implemented since independence.
    • The Plan Holiday was a result of the economic crisis faced by India due to two consecutive years of drought and the Indo-Pak War of 1965.
    • During this period, the government focused on stabilizing the economy and implementing policies to promote self-sufficiency.
    • The Plan Holiday was followed by the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) which focused on poverty alleviation and employment generation.

Additional Information

  • Period of 1990 to 1993:-
    • It refers to the period when India faced a balance of payment crisis and the government implemented economic reforms under the leadership of then-Finance Minister Manmohan Singh. 
  • Period of 1956 to 1960:-
    • It was the Second Five-Year Plan period which focused on industrialization and agriculture.
  • Period of 1947 to 1950:-
    • It  was the immediate post-independence period when the government focused on reconstruction and development.

questions.question: The Green revolution started in the year 1965 and the _______ five-year plan of India was between 1961-66.
questions.questionHtml: The Green revolution started in the year 1965 and the _______ five-year plan of India was between 1961-66.
questions.solution: The Green Revolution in India began in 1965 during the 3rd Five-Year Plan (1961-66). It was initiated under the Ministry of Food and Agriculture led by C. Subramaniam, with Lal Bahadur Shastri as the Prime Minister. M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India, while Norman Borlaug is recognized globally. The term "Green Revolution" was coined by William S. Gaud. It aimed to increase food grain production, particularly wheat and rice, using high-yielding seeds, and to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains, primarily benefiting North Indian states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: The fundamental objective of the second five year plan was to initiate and accelerate the process of ________ so that the development of Indian economy takes a firm base.
questions.questionHtml: The fundamental objective of the second five year plan was to initiate and accelerate the process of ________ so that the development of Indian economy takes a firm base.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is industrialisation.

Key Points

  • The second five-year plan (1956-61) of India was primarily focused on industrialisation to build a self-reliant economy.
  • It was based on the Mahalanobis model, which emphasized the development of heavy industries and capital goods sectors.
  • The plan aimed at reducing import dependency by promoting the establishment of large-scale public sector enterprises.
  • Key industries such as steel, machinery, and heavy engineering received significant investments and support.
  • The plan led to the establishment of major industrial projects like the Bhilai Steel Plant and the Durgapur Steel Plant.

Additional Information

  • Mahalanobis Model
    • Developed by Indian statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, this model laid the framework for the second five-year plan.
    • It emphasized the importance of heavy industry and aimed at a rapid industrialization of the Indian economy.
  • Public Sector Enterprises
    • The second plan focused on the establishment of public sector enterprises in key industries to promote self-sufficiency.
    • PSUs like Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) were established during this period.
  • Heavy Industry
    • Heavy industries include large-scale industries such as steel, machinery, and construction.
    • These industries require significant capital investment and are crucial for building infrastructure.
  • Bhilai and Durgapur Steel Plants
    • The Bhilai Steel Plant was established in collaboration with the Soviet Union.
    • The Durgapur Steel Plant was set up with British collaboration, marking significant industrial milestones.

questions.solution: The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) replaced the Planning Commission in India. It was established on January 1, 2015, as a policy think tank and advisory body to the Government of India. NITI Aayog serves as a platform for formulating and implementing policies and initiatives to promote economic growth, sustainable development, and cooperative federalism in India. It replaced the Planning Commission to bring in a more dynamic and flexible approach to policy-making and to better address the changing needs of the country.

questions.solution: The Eleventh Five-Year Plan in India spanned from 2007 to 2012, focusing on faster and more inclusive growth. Key objectives included poverty reduction, education, health, infrastructure, and environmental sustainability. This plan was among the last formulated by the Planning Commission before it was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015. Five-Year Plans, initiated in 1951 and inspired by the Soviet model, aimed at efficient resource utilization to achieve economic goals. The Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-2017) was the final plan before the Planning Commission's dissolution in 2014.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a reason for emphasizing industrial development in the five year plans?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following was NOT a reason for emphasizing industrial development in the five year plans?

options.text: Industry provides more stable employment than agriculture
options.html: Industry provides more stable employment than agriculture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Industry doesn’t require high investment Key Points

  • One of the key reasons for emphasizing industrial development in the five year plans was that it was seen as a way to promote modernization, overall prosperity, and provide more stable employment compared to agriculture,
  • The idea that industry doesn't require high investment is incorrect; industrial development often necessitates significant capital investment. 
  • Industry promotes modernization:
    • This was a key reason for focusing on industrial development.
    • Industries were seen as a way to modernize the economy by shifting from a primarily agrarian economy to a more diversified one.
    • It also helped in adopting new technologies, production methods, and creating a more robust industrial base.

Additional Information Five-Year Plans:

  • The idea of a five-year plan is simple- The Government of India prepares a document with all its income and expenditure for five years.
  • The budget of the central government and all the state governments is divided into two parts: non-plan and plan budgets.
  • The non-plan budget is spent on routine items yearly. The planned budget is spent on a five-year basis as per the priorities fixed by the plan.
  • The model of the Indian economy was premised on the concept of planning based on five-year plans from 1951 to 2017.
  • The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented, and regulated by a body known as the Planning Commission.
Plan Aim/Goal
First economic development
Second rapid industrialization and the public sector
Third agriculture development and growth
Fourth Growth, Stability, and self-reliance.
Fifth employment and poverty alleviation
Sixth economic liberation 
Seventh Industrial productivity levels through the use of technology
Eighth modernisation of Industries
Ninth elimination of poverty 
Tenth inclusive growth and equitable development
Eleventh rapid and more inclusive growth
Twelfth Faster, More Inclusive, and Sustainable Growth

questions.question: From which five-year plan did India start its journey of industrialisation?
questions.questionHtml: From which five-year plan did India start its journey of industrialisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Second Five-year PlanKey Points

  •  India embarked on its journey of industrialization during the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961) 
  • This plan aimed to put India on the path of industrial growth and development.
  • It focused primarily on heavy industries, including iron and steel, heavy engineering, and fertilizer industries.
  • The three new iron and steel plants were established in Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela during this period.

Additional Information

  •  Third Five-year Plan​
    • The Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966) in India, also known as the “Gadgil Yojna''
    • The Third Plan prioritized improving rice and wheat production. 
    • This scheme started on 1961, and ended on  1966.
  • Fourth Five-year Plan​
    • The scheme started on 1 April 1969 and ended on 31 March 1974.
    • It was a plan based on the Ashok Rudra Menon model.
    • The main objective of this scheme was developed with stability and attainment of economic self-reliance.
    • During this plan period, the slogan of Garibi Hatao was given, which was the original slogan of the 1971 general election.
    • The target of growth rate in this plan was set at 5.7%, while the achievement was only 3.3%.
  • Fifth Five-year Plan 
    • The scheme started on 1 April 1974 and ended on 31 March 1978.
    • The scheme was based on the input-output model.
    • The main objective of this scheme was the eradication of poverty and self-sufficiency.

questions.question: The adoption of the industrial policy of 1956 coincided with which Five-Year Plan?
questions.questionHtml: The adoption of the industrial policy of 1956 coincided with which Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution: The industrial policy of 1956 coincided with India's 2nd Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), which focused on the development of the public sector and rapid industrialization. This policy aimed to establish a socialistic pattern of society by categorizing industries into three schedules: state-owned, progressively state-owned, and private sector. It emphasized the public sector's role in controlling the economy's commanding heights. The 2nd Five-Year Plan, based on the Mahalanobis model, prioritized heavy industries and aimed to increase national and per capita income. Significant projects like the Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela Steel Plants were established during this period.

The plan outlay was Rs 7,98,100 Crores with a target income growth of 3.8% and achieved growth of 4.4%.

The correct answer is Option 1.

Key Points

  • Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79): The key objective was "Garibi Hatao" (Removal of Poverty). This plan aimed to reduce poverty and achieve self-reliance through programs like employment generation and rural development.
  • Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90): Focused on "Food, Work and Productivity" with emphasis on agricultural productivity, employment generation, and human resource development.
  • Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002): Its goal was "Growth with Social Justice and Equality," emphasizing equitable distribution of resources and regional balance.
  • Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12): The objective was "Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth," focusing on inclusive development by reducing disparities in income and opportunities.

Additional Information

  • Five Year Plans: They were centralized economic and social growth strategies in India, initiated in 1951 based on the Soviet model, to enhance development in various sectors.
  • Planning Commission: The institution responsible for drafting and overseeing Five Year Plans in India until it was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.
  • Garibi Hatao Slogan: Introduced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi during the Fifth Five Year Plan to emphasize poverty alleviation as a national priority.
  • Inclusive Growth: Refers to equitable opportunities for economic participants during economic growth, ensuring benefits reach all segments of society, emphasized in the Eleventh Five Year Plan.
  • Transition to NITI Aayog: In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog to adopt a more decentralized approach to planning and policy formulation.

questions.question: The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) was launched during which of the following five year plans?
questions.questionHtml: The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) was launched during which of the following five year plans?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is 6th Five Year Plan.

Key Points

  • The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) was launched during the 6th Five Year Plan (1980–1985).
  • This program was introduced with the aim of providing employment opportunities to rural areas.
  • The NREP was designed to address rural unemployment and promote developmental activities, including the creation of durable community assets like roads, irrigation facilities, and school buildings.
  • The program targeted the poorest segments of the population, ensuring they were included in productive work.
  • The NREP was financed jointly by the Central Government and the State Governments in a ratio of 50:50.
  • It aligned with India's broader strategy to reduce poverty, improve rural infrastructure, and enhance the quality of life in villages.
  • Later, the NREP was merged into the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) in 1989 to streamline rural employment schemes.

 Additional Information

  • 5th Five Year Plan
    • The 5th Five Year Plan (1974–1979) focused on poverty eradication and self-reliance. The major initiative during this period was the introduction of the Minimum Needs Programme.
    • It included schemes for improving education, health, water supply, and housing facilities in rural areas.
    • Although rural employment was addressed indirectly, the NREP was not launched during this plan.
  • 7th Five Year Plan
    • The 7th Five Year Plan (1985–1990) emphasized rapid industrialization, modernization, and enhancing productivity.
    • During this plan, programs like the Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) were expanded, but the NREP had already been initiated earlier in the 6th plan.
  • 8th Five Year Plan
    • The 8th Five Year Plan (1992–1997) focused on human resource development and economic liberalization.
    • By this time, the NREP was merged into other schemes such as the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY).
    • This plan prioritized programs to improve education, health, and employment generation, but the NREP was not launched during this period.

questions.question: Which among the following is/are the objective(s) of setting up of Planning Commission in the 1950s in India? 1. To increase production and offering opportunities to all for employment 2. To make assessment of all resources of the country Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.questionHtml:
Which among the following is/are the objective(s) of setting up of Planning Commission in the 1950s in India?

1. To increase production and offering opportunities to all for employment

2. To make assessment of all resources of the country

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

Key Points

  • The Planning Commission was established in March 1950 to promote a rapid rise in the standard of living of the people by efficient exploitation of the resources of the country.
  • One of the primary objectives was to increase production and provide employment opportunities for all.
  • It was also tasked with making assessments of all resources of the country and formulating plans for their efficient and balanced utilization.
  • The Commission was to determine priorities, define stages of development, and propose the allocation of resources for each stage.
  • It aimed at ensuring an increase in the output of goods and services, to improve the living standards of the people.

Additional Information

  • The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
  • The Commission was headed by the Prime Minister of India and had a Deputy Chairman, appointed by the Prime Minister.
  • The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused on the agricultural sector, and aimed to address the immediate problem of food shortages and inflation.
  • In 2014, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), which serves as the policy think tank of the Government of India.
  • The NITI Aayog aims to involve the states in economic policy-making in India and to promote cooperative federalism.

questions.question: On which date was the National Development Council set up?
questions.questionHtml: On which date was the National Development Council set up?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is 6th August 1952.

Key Points

  • The National Development Council (NDC) was set up on 6th August 1952 by a resolution of the Government of India.
  • The NDC is an important part of the planning process in India and plays a key role in the approval of plans formulated by the Planning Commission (now replaced by the NITI Aayog).
  • It serves as the highest decision-making authority for socio-economic planning in India.
  • The council includes the Prime Minister of India, Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States and Union Territories, and members of the Planning Commission.
  • The primary objective of the NDC is to promote cooperation between the central and state governments and to ensure the implementation of national plans effectively.
  • It also reviews the progress of plans and suggests measures to achieve the objectives of rapid economic development and balanced regional growth.
  • The establishment of the NDC marks a significant step in the development of decentralized planning and the involvement of states in national policy-making.

 Additional Information

  • Planning Commission:
    • The Planning Commission, established in 1950, was responsible for formulating India's five-year plans.
    • The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
    • Its role was to assess resources, formulate strategies for economic growth, and allocate resources effectively.
  • NITI Aayog:
    • The NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is a policy think tank established by the Government of India in 2015.
    • It replaced the Planning Commission to foster a more decentralized and participative approach to governance.
    • It focuses on policy formulation, fostering cooperative federalism, and enhancing innovation and research.
